{1}. Compilation engagement
Objective and scope.

You have asked us to perform a compilation engagement for the Company for {1}. In a compilation engagement, we assist management in preparing financial information. The compiled financial information will be {2} (the “compiled financial information”).

The compiled financial information is intended to be used by management of the Company, and to support the Company’s corporate income tax return filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). CRA is in a position to request and obtain further information from the Company.
You confirm that {1} has agreed with you the basis of accounting to be applied.
You confirm that {1} is in a position to request and obtain further information from the Company.
It will also be provided to {1}. {2}

If you plan to give the compiled financial information to anyone else, such as a lender or landlord, please tell us first. It should only be given to a party that is in a position to request and obtain further information from the Company, or that has agreed with you the basis of accounting applied.
Intended use.

The compiled financial information will be prepared using the basis of accounting required by {1}. It will not apply all the requirements of Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises (ASPE).
Basis of accounting.
{1} Note 1 to the compiled financial information will describe this basis. If your needs change during the engagement and a different basis is needed, we will agree the change with you in writing.
Our responsibilities.

We will perform the engagement in accordance with Canadian Standard on Related Services (CSRS) 4200, Compilation Engagements. CSRS 4200 requires us to comply with relevant ethical requirements, including the CPA Ontario Code of Professional Conduct. We will use our accounting and financial reporting expertise to help you prepare and present the compiled financial information. We will discuss with you any significant judgments on which we assist. We will read the compiled financial information in light of what we know about the Company and the basis of accounting. If it appears to be misleading, we will ask you for additional or corrected information. If it is not provided, we will withdraw from the engagement and tell you why.

A compilation engagement is not an audit or a review. We will not verify the accuracy or completeness of the information you give us. We will not express an audit opinion or a review conclusion, or provide any form of assurance on the compiled financial information. This engagement cannot be relied on to detect errors, fraud or illegal acts. The Code of Professional Conduct does not require us to be independent of the Company for this engagement. If we are not independent, our report will say so.
By signing this letter, management acknowledges that:
a compilation engagement is appropriate for the intended use described above;
a compilation engagement is not an audit or a review, and will not meet any legal, regulatory or contractual requirement for an audit or a review; and

the compiled financial information should not be used by third parties other than those who are in a position to request and obtain further information from the Company, or who have agreed with you the basis of accounting applied.
Management is responsible for:
the compiled financial information;
selecting a basis of accounting that is appropriate for the intended use;
the accuracy and completeness of the records, documents, explanations and other information given to us;
keeping proper books and records and internal controls, and giving us access to them and to the people we need to speak with; and
attaching our compilation engagement report whenever the compiled financial information is distributed or reproduced.
Before we issue our report, management will confirm in writing that it takes responsibility for the final version of the compiled financial information.

It is not our report and must not be used, copied or attached to any financial information. There may be circumstances in which the report differs from its expected form and content, based on our findings during the engagement.

Timely performance

Concept Accounting will use all reasonable efforts to complete the services described in the engagement letter within any agreed time frame. Concept Accounting is not liable for failures or delays caused by matters beyond its control, including the Company not meeting its obligations under the engagement letter on time.
Right to end the engagement

The Company may end the engagement on 30 days’ written notice. The Company will then pay for time and expenses incurred up to the end date, and for reasonable time and expenses needed to bring the services to an orderly close. If the Company does not meet its obligations under this Agreement and does not fix the default within 30 days after receiving notice from Concept Accounting, Concept Accounting may end the engagement by written notice, without prejudice to its other rights. In that case, Concept Accounting is not responsible for any loss, cost, expense or damage resulting from ending the engagement.
Change Order

If the Company needs a significant change to the services after the date of the engagement letter, the change must be agreed in writing in a Change Order. The Change Order will set out the revised services and any added fees.
Fees

Any fee estimate assumes the agreed level of preparation and help from the Company’s personnel. Concept Accounting will tell management promptly if that help is not provided, or if anything else will cause the work to take longer than estimated.
Billing

Invoices are due on receipt. Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice first. If a scheduled payment is not received, Concept Accounting may pause work until it is. Concept Accounting may charge interest on any balance unpaid for more than 30 days at 1.5% per month (19.56% per year).
Taxes
Fees and other charges do not include GST/HST or any other sales or similar taxes, now in force or imposed later. The Company will pay these taxes in addition to the fees.
Governing law

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Province of Ontario and the federal laws of Canada that apply in Ontario. It is an Ontario contract. The Company and Concept Accounting submit to the courts of Ontario for all matters arising under this Agreement.
Working papers

Concept Accounting owns all working papers, files, materials, reports and work it creates during the engagement, including the intellectual property used to prepare them. Concept Accounting will give management a copy of any working papers it prepares that are needed for the Company’s accounting records. Any tools Concept Accounting gives the Company, such as spreadsheets, are provided as is, at its discretion, and must not be shared with any third party. Except as required by the Code of Professional Conduct or by law, Concept Accounting is not required to share its working papers with the Company or anyone else.
Personal information

The Company will not give Concept Accounting any personal information, as defined in Canadian federal and provincial privacy laws, except as needed for the services. If personal information is collected, used or disclosed by Concept Accounting, the Company consents to this and confirms that it has obtained all consents and given all notices required by law. Concept Accounting will handle personal information under its privacy policy (conceptaccounting.ca/privacy-policy) and in line with applicable Canadian privacy laws.
Confidentiality

Concept Accounting will not disclose the Company’s confidential information to any third party without the Company’s consent, except: (a) when properly acting in the course of the services, including to its subcontractors and advisors who need to know; (b) as required by law or permitted by professional standards; or (c) where the information is or becomes public other than through a breach by Concept Accounting, is disclosed by the Company to a third party without similar restrictions, is received by Concept Accounting from another source without a duty of confidence, was already known to Concept Accounting, or is developed by Concept Accounting independently. The Company acknowledges that Concept Accounting’s files, including the files for this engagement, may be reviewed by practice inspectors of CPA Ontario, and of any other provincial CPA body that regulates Concept Accounting, as required by law and professional standards. Those inspectors are bound by confidentiality.
Data analytics

Concept Accounting may use the information the Company gives it during the engagement (“Client Data”) to prepare reports for the Company alone, and to prepare aggregated benchmarking and industry reports using de-identified data. Aggregated reports will not contain any information that would allow a third party to identify the Company, and de-identified data will not be re-identified.
Release and limitation of liability

(a) In any claim arising out of the engagement, Concept Accounting’s liability is several and not joint, and the Company may only recover Concept Accounting’s proportionate share of the total liability, based on its degree of fault as finally determined by a court. (b) Except for matters finally determined to result from Concept Accounting’s gross negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct, and whether the claim is in contract, tort or otherwise: (i) Concept Accounting is not liable for, and the Company releases it from, all claims, damages, costs and expenses (including legal fees) arising out of the engagement to the extent they exceed the total professional fees paid by the Company to Concept Accounting for this engagement in the 12 months starting on the date of the engagement letter; and (ii) Concept Accounting is not liable for any consequential, indirect or lost profit damages, or for any failure to realize expected savings.
Indemnity

The Company will indemnify and hold Concept Accounting harmless against: (a) all claims, damages, costs and expenses (including legal fees) arising out of the engagement, whether civil, penal, regulatory or administrative, except those finally determined by a court to result from Concept Accounting’s gross negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct; and (b) despite (a), all claims, damages, costs and expenses (including legal fees) arising out of the engagement that result from any deliberate misstatement or omission in any information or representation supplied or approved by any officer or director of the Company.
Meaning of Concept Accounting

In the Release and Limitation of Liability clause and the Indemnity clause, “Concept Accounting” means Concept Accounting & Advisory Professional Corporation and its directors, officers, employees, contractors and agents, and any successor or assignee.
Survival
The Release and Limitation of Liability clause, the Indemnity clause, the Confidentiality clause and the Working Papers clause continue to apply after the engagement ends.
Electronic communications

Unless the Company asks in writing for a particular method, Concept Accounting will communicate in the way it considers most efficient, which will often be email and secure client portals. Neither party controls the performance, reliability or security of the internet. Concept Accounting is not liable for any loss or damage caused by delay, interception, corruption, security breach or failed delivery of any communication sent outside Concept Accounting’s own systems.
Third-party services

Concept Accounting may use third parties, including team members and service providers located outside Canada, for professional, administrative and support services. Client Data may therefore be stored, used or accessed outside the Company’s province or outside Canada, where it may be subject to the laws of that jurisdiction. Concept Accounting requires these third parties to keep Client Data confidential on terms equivalent to this Agreement. Concept Accounting is not responsible for any third-party product or service the Company obtains on its own, even if Concept Accounting helped to arrange it.

Dear [ACCOUNT_NAME],

Thank you for choosing Concept Accounting for your personal income tax. This letter sets out the services we will provide, your responsibilities and ours, and how our fees work. Please read it and sign it to confirm.
This letter applies to your current tax year and to each later year we prepare your return, until either of us ends it in writing.

We will prepare and electronically file your T1 Income Tax and Benefit Return. If your spouse or common-law partner is also included under this letter, we will prepare their return too, and each of you must sign.

Each return will include the schedules and forms that apply to you, based on the information you give us. These can include employment and investment income, self-employment or commission income (Form T2125), rental properties (Form T776), foreign property reporting (Form T1135), and the sale of property, including the principal residence designation where it applies.

GST/HST returns. If you have self-employment income and we prepare your GST/HST return, we prepare it from the information you give us. We do not audit or verify it. You are responsible for keeping the records that support your claims and for any tax, interest or penalties if CRA disallows a claim.
We prepare your return from the information and documents you give us through your tax organizer. We do not audit or verify that information, although we may ask you to clarify it.
2. Your responsibilities
giving us complete and accurate information, including all tax slips, receipts and records, before we start;

confirming that the expenses you claim are supported by records and are not personal, such as haircuts, vacations, household costs or personal vehicle use, because personal expenses cannot be deducted;
keeping your records and supporting documents for the period the Income Tax Act requires, as CRA may ask for them;
reviewing your return carefully before you sign Form T183, because you have final responsibility for your return; and
Our work cannot be relied on to prevent or detect fraud, errors or omissions. That responsibility stays with you.
3. CRA access

We need Level 2 online access to your CRA information to prepare your return. Your tax organizer explains how to give it. We start work once access is in place. You can cancel our access at any time in your CRA account.
4. Filing and deadlines
When your return is ready, we will send you Form T183. You must review the return and sign Form T183 before we can file it.

Returns are due April 30 of the year after the tax year. If you or your spouse or common-law partner had self-employment income, the filing deadline is June 15, but any balance owing is still due April 30. Late filing and late payment can result in penalties and interest.
5. Fees and payment
Your fee is set from your answers to our scope questions, using our fee schedule. It is one fee for the year's return.
Before we start: we send your fee by invoice with this letter. The invoice is paid before we begin work.

If your return changes: if you give us something that was not in your scope answers, for example a rental property, a property sale, foreign property or self-employment income, we quote the added fee to you in writing first. We only go ahead once you accept it.
Late or changed information: if you send slips or information after we have prepared your return and we must redo part of it, we quote the added fee before we do that work.
Release and filing: we file your return, and release it to you, once your invoice is paid.

Payment: you pay online through your secure client portal. GST/HST is added to each invoice. Invoices are due on receipt. Interest may be charged on balances unpaid for more than 30 days at 1.5% per month (19.56% per year).
Questions about your return are included in your fee.
Legal requests: if a law, regulator or court requires us to produce our files or answer requests about your return, we bill the time and costs involved.
6. What is not included
This letter does not include:
CRA reviews, audits, objections or representation;
tax planning or advice;
prior-year returns;
bookkeeping, or GST/HST returns unless you ask for them;
payroll, EHT, WSIB or other taxes and levies;
foreign income tax returns or advice on foreign taxes.
If you ask for any of these, we will quote them in writing first.

Unless you ask us to prepare your GST/HST return, we do not review your GST/HST. We may not notice if GST/HST is being collected or claimed incorrectly. Errors can lead to tax, interest and penalties.
7. Foreign property and foreign reporting
CRA requires information returns, with significant penalties for filing late or not filing, if at any time in the year you:
held specified foreign property, such as foreign bank accounts, foreign real estate or shares of foreign companies, costing more than $100,000 in total;
owned at least 10% of a foreign company, alone or together with related persons; or
sent money or property to, received money or property from, or were owed money by a non-resident trust, including an inheritance from a foreign estate.
You agree to answer the foreign property questions in your tax organizer completely and to tell us about any of these each year.
8. Our judgment

Tax law is not always clear. Where it is unclear, we use our professional judgment to choose a supportable position. Our conclusions are matters of professional opinion, not certainty. CRA may not agree, and you have rights of appeal if it proposes changes.
9. Your information and confidentiality

We collect, use and keep your personal information only to provide our services, under our privacy policy (conceptaccounting.ca/privacy-policy) and Canadian privacy laws. If you give us information about another person, such as a spouse or dependant, you confirm you have their consent.

We keep your information confidential and release it only with your consent or as the law requires. Our files may be reviewed by practice inspectors of CPA Ontario, as professional standards require; those inspectors are bound by confidentiality.
Our team includes members and service providers located outside Canada, so your information may be stored or accessed outside Canada, under confidentiality terms equal to ours.
10. Electronic communications

We communicate by email and through our secure client portal. No one fully controls the security of the internet. We are not liable for loss caused by delay, interception or failed delivery of messages sent outside our own systems.
11. Limitation of liability

Our liability for any claim arising from this engagement, whether in contract, tort or otherwise, is limited to the fees you paid us for the return in question. It does not cover consequential or indirect losses. Our liability is several and not joint: you may only recover our share of any loss, based on our degree of fault. We are not responsible for interest or penalties caused by information that was late, incomplete or inaccurate.
12. Ending this agreement and governing law
Either of us may end this agreement in writing. You will pay for work done up to that date. We may withdraw before filing if we cannot complete the work, and we will tell you why.
This agreement is governed by the laws of Ontario, and the courts of Ontario have jurisdiction over any dispute.
By signing below, you confirm that this letter reflects your understanding and that we may proceed.
